item.description: Tom Newbold was living the dream, his friends said. He met friends at Dumont Dunes west of Las Vegas and embraced a love for sand and speed that eventually ended his life.

item.title: Southwest Gas proposes 2.8% increase; public invited to comment
item.description: LAS VEGAS (KLAS) — Southwest Gas Corporation wants to increase the rates it charges consumers. Under Nevada law, natural gas utilities must file an annual adjustment application to determine whether customers are overpaying or underpaying for gas costs. item.title: Nevada casinos win $1.3 billion in January; Las Vegas Strip takes nearly $750 million
item.description: Nevada casinos won $1.3 billion from gamblers in January, a 6.5% decrease compared to January 2025. Record months at the end of 2024 skew the comparisons.

item.title: Las Vegas visitors down 2.2% in January, LVCVA reports
item.description: Las Vegas tourism was slower in January than it was a year ago as visitors declined by 2.2%. The decline was less than many months through 2025, when economic uncertainty from tariffs put the brakes on travel.

item.title: 'Come volunteer': Non-profit helps Nevadans at risk of losing SNAP
item.description: Approximately 44,000 Nevadans are at risk of losing their SNAP benefits. Starting March 1, SNAP recipients will have to meet new requirements to keep their benefits. Able-bodied adults, without dependents, must complete 20 hours of approved work activities or risk losing assistance.

item.title: When We Were Young music festival announces 2026 hiatus
item.description: The annual When We Were Young music festival that features bands like My Chemical Romance, Blink 182 and Panic! at the Disco announced that it will not be happening in 2026.

item.title: Family of boy slain during Las Vegas police shooting plans to sue Metro
item.description: The family of a young boy shot and killed during an incident involving police and the boy's father plans to sue the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department, the family said Friday.
